sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 880.1 ± 72.4 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-FLAG ICC confirmed surface-accessible localization of GPR63 in NIH 3T3 cells; no functional (signaling) assay reported in these clips.
sites.rationale: L3 explicitly states GPR63-TANGO-FLAG carries an N-terminal FLAG tag; the topology landmarks place residues 1–83 extracellular with no signal peptide, so the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus and the tag must be prepended (insert_after_residue = 0, residue_after = M). Python confirmed residue 1 = M and that TM1 begins at residue 84, leaving 83 residues of extracellular N-terminal space. The TANGO vector system (Barnea et al.) is established for N-terminal FLAG tagging of GPCRs at exactly this position. L4 confirms anti-FLAG ICC detected the construct at the cell surface. GPR63-TANGO-FLAG construct expresses human GPR63 with an N-terminal FLAG tag under CMV promoter control, transfected into NIH 3T3 cells; anti-FLAG immunocytochemistry was used to detect GPR63 localization (L3, L4).

sources.claim: GPR63-TANGO-FLAG is a plasmid designed to express human GPR63 with an N-terminal FLAG tag under the control of a CMV promoter from a Tango vector [ 48 ].

literature_notes: Four ledger lines were examined. L1 and L4 are supporting context (transfection and ICC protocol) and do not independently pin a new site. L3 grounds the N-terminal FLAG site. L2 reports a C-terminal myc-DDK tag; the C-terminus of GPR63 falls in the intracellular domain (residues 374–419 per topology landmarks), so this tag is on the cytoplasmic face and is recorded in other_positions only. No ledger line reports a tag in any extracellular loop (ECL1 139–155, ECL2 216–242, ECL3 337–351), so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: pCMV6-GPR63-myc carries a myc-DDK tag at the C-terminus of GPR63; the C-terminus (residues 374–419) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface-tag site.
